About DEVCON Philippines

A non-profit built by volunteers since 2009.

DEVCON Philippines (DevConnect Philippines Inc.) is the country’s largest and longest-running volunteer tech community, an SEC-registered, BIR-compliant non-profit for developers, IT students, educators, and tech enthusiasts.

In 2026 we celebrate our 17th anniversary with 13 locations nationwide, all working toward one vision: a technology-empowered Philippines for all.

  • Non-profit since 2009
  • SEC-registered and BIR-compliant
  • 17th anniversary in 2026

Home/Our Story
Our 17-year AI narrative

Seventeen years ago, a group of Filipino developers decided that technology should not be reserved for the few.

Fast forward to 2026: 13 locations, a 60,000+ strong network, and 120+ free events every year.

About us

One nationwide community. 13 locations.

DEVCON is the Philippines' largest volunteer tech community and non-profit for developers, IT enthusiasts, and future geeks. We promote the collaborative growth and global competence of Filipino developers, giving everyone from Luzon to Visayas to Mindanao a place to Sync, Support, and Succeed.

  1. 1

    Hosting unconferences for IT students, professionals, and educators since 2009, with local chapters serving as regional community hubs from Pampanga to Davao.

  2. 2

    Organizing hackathons, code camps, and innovation challenges with universities, enterprises, and government agencies.

  3. 3

    Hosting the DEVCON Summit since 2013, with sessions on open source, web3, AI, data science, and the future of work.

How we got here

Seventeen years, one idea.

  1. 2009

    The first DEVCON

    Unconferences for IT students, professionals, and educators. Free, volunteer-run, open to all.

  2. 2013

    DEVCON Summit begins

    A national stage for open source, web3, AI, data science, and the future of work.

  3. Growth

    From Luzon to Mindanao

    Chapters and volunteer communities become local tech hubs, today in 13 locations nationwide.

  4. 2025

    Builders at scale

    70k+ reached online, 19k+ face-to-face, and 800+ smart contracts deployed to mainnet.

  5. 2026

    Engineering an AI-Ready Nation

    Our 17th year puts AI skills in the hands of every Filipino builder, from kids to leaders.

The formula

Institutions aligned. The rest is ours to build.

DEVCON, Amihan and Avtica, and DOST signed an MOU to deliver the formula together.

  • Human capital

    DEVCON

    Peer learning at national scale, global certifications, and AI Certification Scholarships for the first wave of Filipino FDEs.

  • Platforms

    Amihan and Avtica

    Democratizing access to AI, so emerging nations can tap the world's best models, tools, and agents.

  • Infrastructure

    DOST

    National compute, R&D funding, and the rails for science and entrepreneurship.

Nationwide chapters

Empowering local tech leaders and communities nationwide

13 locations across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao, with 120+ free events every year.

Quality over quantity

We grow chapters, not pins on a map.

A DEVCON chapter is more than a location. It needs active officers, regular local programs, and shared standards. Communities without active officers yet stay local tech community networks until they’re ready to become chapters.

  • Active local leaders

    Elected officers who run the chapter and lead its local partnerships.

  • Consistent programs

    Regular meetups, code camps, and campus events, not one-off visits.

  • Shared standards

    Every chapter follows the Playbook, Code of Conduct, and Child Protection Policy.

DevRel case study · Build Beyond

From robotics to smart contracts: building beyond Manila with Sui

In March 2026, the Sui Foundation and DEVCON Philippines launched a year-long partnership to help educators, IT students, and developers code in Move on Sui, delivered through DEVCON’s nationwide chapters and regional hubs.

Year 1 results so far

Five chapters. 330+ contracts on mainnet.

  • 548Code camp attendees across 5 chapters
  • 330+Verified submissions on Sui mainnet plus a public Vercel app
  • 60.4%Completion rate vs. registered attendees
  • 6Developer events alongside the camps
The challenge

Tech moves faster than classrooms can

The global tech landscape evolves faster than academic programs can adapt. Filipino students and developers outside Metro Manila often get the least access to hands-on emerging-tech training.

“We must provide immediate community support to Filipino developers to stay ready for what’s next.”

Dom De Leon, Executive Director, DEVCON Philippines
Step 1 · Start early

From robotics to smart contracts

Sui donated AI-lensed robotics kits and micro:bits to DEVCON Kids. Students at Iloilo National High School are already building interactive, creative robotics, and the support has reached learners in Pangasinan and Iloilo.

The goal, in the words of DEVCON Kids Founder Pam Ros Damarillo: lower the intimidation factor of tech and turn curiosity into a career path.

Step 2 · Proof of learning

Code camps that end on mainnet

The Move Smart Contracts Code Camps launched at Colegio de San Juan de Letran’s College of Engineering and IT during the She Is DEVCON celebrations. The camps are free, hands-on, and help educators bring emerging tech into their own classes.

Every participant deploys a Move smart contract on Sui mainnet and ships a public Vercel app, so their authorship is immutable and verifiable.

Step 3 · Go nationwide

Manila first, then the regions

After Manila, the camps rolled out through local chapters and partner schools in Bukidnon, Iloilo, Laguna, and Legazpi, alongside AI-era developer events from Makati to Mindanao. Mysten Labs Developer Advocate Harrison Kim framed the aim: give builders the right tools for a world shaped by AI, backed by strong local community support.

Code camp results

Results by chapter

ChapterDateAttendeesVerifiedIncompleteCompletion
ManilaMar 28128293122.66%
BukidnonMay 613673752.94%
IloiloMay 161641441986.59%
LagunaMay 298056470.00%
LegazpiJul 304029372.50%
Total548330+6460.40%

Manila was the pilot. Delivery improved rapidly after every code camp: completion climbed from 22.7% in Manila to 52.9% in Bukidnon, then 86.6% in Iloilo, and held at 70%+ in Laguna and Legazpi.

Timeline and KPIs

A year-long rollout, reported quarterly

  1. Q4 2025DEVCON Kids micro:bit donation (25 kits) and Hour of AI support
  2. Q1 2026Partnership launch and kickoff, mentor training batch 1, first code camp, Q1 report
  3. Q2 2026Mentor training batch 2, SheIsDEVCON events, code camps 2 to 4, DEVCON 17 feature, Q2 report
  4. Q3 2026Code camp 5, DEVCON Studios features, Q3 report
  5. Q4 2026Final report and assessment
What it means

Builders, not spectators

Build Beyond makes the first moves, from AI robotics for youth to blockchain for students, free and local. By reaching past Manila to Visayas and Mindanao chapters, it helps Filipinos become active builders of the future, not just spectators of it.

2025 chapter story

Five high-impact events at the center

Elevate and Empowher: She is DEVCON × UXPH inspired hundreds of women toward leadership in development and design. The chapter spotlighted iThink Hackathon finalists at Philippine Blockchain Week, and took its mission global at WOCEE. DevRel case study · ICP Philippines

The biggest smart contracts code camp series in the Philippines

With ISLA CAMP (ICP HUB Philippines), DEVCON runs a nationwide smart contracts builder education advocacy and code camps, taking blockchain training to schools and cities that rarely get it.

Series results

Reach, then real deployments

  • 200,000+Online reach of ICP-supported events and content
  • 3,000+Students and developers reached offline
  • 700+Developers engaged in hands-on code camps
  • 500+Smart contract projects completed and deployed
  • 60+ schools and partners
  • 56% average deployment completion
  • 80+ trained mentors nationwide
  • 30+ training sessions and code camps
  • 10+ underserved and new tech communities
  • 2 major summits

The approach

Go where the opportunities aren’t

The series focuses on underserved and new tech communities, so students can publish their first smart contract as part of their portfolio.

  • Mindoro
  • Lucena
  • Leyte
  • Baguio
  • Tagum
  • Bukidnon
  • General Santos

Two major summits anchored the series: the Mindanao Summit in Davao and the CALABARZON Summit in Lipa.

The partner’s goal

From technology consumers to active builders

For ISLA CAMP founder Nelson Lumbres, the partnership gives Filipino developers a way to stand out globally and reach transformative opportunities.

The bigger outcome

Code camps that grow chapters

The camps helped DEVCON build and support new chapters in Laguna, Bukidnon, and Pampanga.

“Empowering the builder community to be future-ready and decentralizing access to tech opportunities.”

Dom De Leon, Executive Director, DEVCON Philippines

This partnership covers emerging-technology education and code camps only. It is not financial advice on cryptocurrency.

Open-Source AI Code Camps · Barangay AI

Build your own AI. 100% free and open-sourced.

At the Barangay AI Beta Code Camp on August 27, 2026, 19 builders went from “what is an LLM” to a live, public AI in one afternoon, on ordinary computers, with zero cloud spend required.

See the AI showcase (opens in a new tab)Explore the platform (opens in a new tab)
Beta results

Everyone finished. Everyone would come back.

Part of a nationwide push: 500+ builders trained on AI Fluency, and growing.

  • 100%Completion: all 19 builders finished all 19 verified steps
  • 100%Would tell a friend to join the next one
  • 89%Plan to keep building on their AI
  • 19Builders, each shipping a solo build
How the camp works

Four sprints. Nineteen verified steps.

A step-by-step checklist walks every builder from installing Ollama to shipping a live AI. Every step is time-boxed, auto-verified, and carries proof of work and facilitator notes, with no separate forms.

  1. 1

    Understand and fork

    Learn how LLMs work, then fork the Barangay AI repo.

  2. 2

    Run it locally

    Install Ollama and pull an open-weight model on your own machine.

  3. 3

    Customize

    Give your AI a name, a persona, a reply language, and your own documents.

  4. 4

    Publish

    Connect it to a real chat app and ship a live public URL.

Open the Code Camp Checklist (opens in a new tab)
Build with open source

Ollama, GitHub, and Vercel. Free, no cloud needed.

Future-ready developers know how to pick the right tools and build with open source. Every builder forked the Barangay AI app and ran it on their own machine.

  • Local-first AI chat

    Talks to a model running on your own machine through Ollama. Your chats never leave your device.

  • Speaks your language

    Replies in English, Filipino, Taglish, Bisaya, Hiligaynon, or Ilocano.

  • Shows its receipts

    Grounded on your own files, with the exact source behind every answer.

  • Works offline

    Once loaded, the only thing it needs is your model.

    See the code on GitHub (opens in a new tab)

What they built

Personal, grounded in real documents, and live

Personas

  • 6 companions like Liv AI, TALI, SKAD, and Gon
  • 5 study tutors like Master Shifu, Auren, and Bagbag AI
  • 4 personal builds made to tinker with
  • 2 barangay assistants, including Pare Santiago for Brgy. Santiago
  • 2 culture builds, ChizMakers and JaysonTheGrasscutter

Grounded in real files

  • 19 of 19 brought their own document, nobody tested on a sample
  • Coursework: Circuit Theory, UI/UX prep, ITEC-85
  • Live projects: a CocoFiber capstone and Operation Longshot
  • Civic paperwork: a barangay consent form, queried in Tagalog
Models and choices

Open-weight models, served locally with Ollama

The top two models powered 84% of all builds. 16 of 19 builders picked the 1B to 3B size band; 3 sized up to 7B–8B.

Models chosen by builders

  • qwen2.5:3b14 builders · 73.7%
  • llama3.1:8b2 builders · 10.5%
  • qwen2.5:1.5b1 builder · 5.3%
  • gemma3:4b1 builder · 5.3%
  • qwen2.5:0.5b1 builder · 5.3%

Reply language configured

One in four replied in Filipino or Taglish.

  • English14
  • Taglish3
  • Filipino2

Cloud providers added

Optional, by the 5 builders who added a cloud key.

  • DeepSeek5
  • Groq4
  • OpenAI1

Every OS finished with no drop-off: 16 of 19 built on Windows, alongside macOS and Linux.

Retrospective

What worked, and where we’ll focus next

What worked

  • 100% completion across all 19 verified steps
  • 100% positive sentiment: every builder would tell a friend
  • 84% said the pace felt about right
  • 79% of those who got stuck were unstuck within minutes
  • 89% plan to keep building after the camp
  • Windows, macOS, and Linux all finished with no drop-off

Where to improve

  • Sprint 3 (Customize) was the hardest step for 42% of builders
  • Pre-install and local setup caused 37% of early friction
  • Pace was polarizing for a few: 2 said too fast, 1 too slow
  • More roaming facilitators, so no one falls behind
  • Clearer prompts so app versions aren’t mistaken for model names

DEVCON Jumpstart · AI Engineering Internships

Your tech career launchpad, now on an AI Engineering track

Cohort 5 puts top students on an AI Engineering track: five months of mentorship from Amihan and Avtica engineers, building real AI solutions for national-scale challenges with Claude, NVIDIA Orin, and Qwen.

Apply for the next cohortSee the tracks
Cohort 5

Program at a glance

  • Cohort 5Now on an AI Engineering track
  • 5 monthsTo build a portfolio of real projects
  • 8 tracksMix and match your top 2
  • 1–2In-person sessions a week at the HQ office in Makati or Ortigas
Two ways to join

Voluntary or for school credit. Your call.

Jumpstart works as a voluntary internship or as your academic internship, OJT, or practicum requirement.

Most of our interns

Voluntary adventure learning

The majority of our interns join voluntarily, on top of school, to explore, build, and get industry-ready before they graduate. No grade required, just curiosity and commitment.

  • Learn beyond the curriculum
  • Build a portfolio of real AI projects
  • Meet mentors and the industry early
Also available

Academic requirement

Need internship hours for your degree? Jumpstart can count toward your school’s internship, OJT, or practicum requirement. Tell us your school’s requirements when you apply.

  • Structured five-month program
  • Mentor supervision and documented outputs
  • Coordination with your school on requirements
The AI Engineering track

Build AI that the country can actually use

Forget the typical internship. Jumpstart focuses on your growth, with mentors who push you to see bigger opportunities in tech. On the AI Engineering track, you ship working AI for DEVCON’s nationwide community, not practice exercises.

  • Amihan and Avticaengineers as your mentors
  • Anthropic Claudefor building with frontier AI
  • NVIDIA Orinfor AI at the edge
  • Qwenfor open-weight models

    Practical tips and guidance from pros, in a supportive space that values your ideas.

  • Mentorship and guidance

    Grow teamwork, communication, and problem-solving, with outputs for your job applications.

  • Flexible learning

    Online, in-person, and expert sessions across diverse tracks and modules.

  • Professional development

    Confidence beyond tech, plus special recognition for stand-out work.

  • Real-world experience

    Travel to events, visit institutions, and work on projects that mirror industry.

Program structure

How the five months work

  • Flexible learning

    Asynchronous learning blended with in-person expert talks and mentorship.

  • In-person sessions

    1–2 sessions a week at the DEVCON HQ office in Makati or Ortigas, plus best-in-class conferences.

  • Exclusive tech events

    Workshops, on-site events, and career-accelerating access across the DEVCON community.

  • Guest speaker sessions

    Industry experts, each followed by an “Ask Me Anything”.

  • Transportation and communication allowance

    Provided by DEVCON throughout the internship.

From our interns

In their words

  • “I walked in asking, “Why me?” I walked out thinking, “Why not me?””

    Ivy · Jumpstart intern

  • “The projects I worked on weren’t just exercises; they were tools that could actually be deployed and used.”

    David · Jumpstart intern

  • “I committed to showing up, delivering results, and learning as much as I could.”

    Anj · BS IT, PLM Manila, Cohort 1

  • “It equipped me with new skill sets that seamlessly integrate with my existing freelance tech stack.”

    AJ · BS IT, Bulacan State University, Cohort 1

  • “DEVCON has shown me that with the right support, I can overcome my perceived limitations.”

    Eizel · BS IT, Bulacan State University, Cohort 1

  • “I thought I’d spend my time in Canva and Photoshop, but instead I was pulled into the wider world of tech.”

    Lewis · Cohort 2
FAQ

Before you apply

Is it voluntary, or can it count for school?

Both. Most of our interns join voluntarily as adventure learning, to be ready for the industry. It can also count toward your academic internship, OJT, or practicum requirement; tell us your school’s requirements when you apply.

Is this a paid internship?

It is unpaid, but DEVCON provides transportation and communication allowances.

What is the time commitment?

Five months of online, self-paced learning plus 1–2 in-person sessions a week, and occasional on-site and chapter events.

Where are the in-person sessions?

At the DEVCON HQ office in Makati or Ortigas. We’ll confirm the venue before each session. The cohort agrees on Tuesdays or Thursdays.

What do I submit?

Your CV, and a cover letter with your top 2 tracks, top 3 skills, 2–3 relevant projects, 2–3 favorite tech events, and how you learned about DEVCON.

How does selection work?

Slots are limited and selection is competitive. Shortlisted applicants are invited for an office visit and notified within 1–2 weeks. Not shortlisted? Re-apply to a future cohort.

Which tracks are available?

Tracks depend on instructor availability and each cohort’s priorities. You pick a top 2, and you’re encouraged to collaborate on other projects.

Limited slots. Competitive selection.

Do you have what it takes? Tell us why.

2025 chapter story

Investing in kids to build an ecosystem

Iloilo ran 32 events and reached 4,833 people in 2025: 45% college students, 39% elementary and high school students, and 16% adults and professionals, its strongest professional turnout yet.

Highlights include SheIsDEVCON / CoDHER workshops for 100+ young women with DEPDEV GAD and DICT, the Tech Awards for student leaders, the GAME ON indie game competition built on Iloilo’s heritage with DOST Region 6 and the Iloilo City Government, and the four-day Tech4All Summit, run entirely through partners and volunteers.

Hour of AI #RoadTo1KYouths brought hands-on AI training to 1,680+ kids across 15 sessions in urban and rural public schools, with the Iloilo City and Provincial Governments.

2025 chapter story

Technology with compassion, for every sector

Bukidnon ran 37 events in 2025, reaching out-of-school youth, freelancers, MSME owners, students, educators, and Indigenous learners. BukFest 2025 alone gathered 6,000+ participants over a week of 12 main events, tailored for agriculture, business, education, culture, the arts, and music.

At She is DEVCON: Shertified, the chapter launched MAVIC with the GAD Office, a system that helps partner agencies monitor cases of abused women, alongside an ICP code camp. Through Bits of Light, volunteers brought tech education and care services to Indigenous learners of Luyungan Farm School, a school for children rescued from child labor and early marriage, and helped parents travel from their villages to join.

Next: adopting the school under the 2026 DEVCON Bukidnon Tech Series, “From Basics to Brilliance”, starting with teacher training so tech experts stay in the school community.

Community Playbook

Volunteering Basics and Best Practices

A first-timer’s guide to volunteering at a DEVCON chapter event. If you got your confirmation, congratulations: we’re thrilled to have you on board.

On this page

  • Who we are
  • What to expect
  • What to bring
  • Before the event
  • On the day
  • After the event
  • Best practices from our 13 locations
  • Event rescheduling and weather protocol

Who we are

DEVCON is a registered non-profit dedicated to empowering IT students and professionals nationwide. For 17 years, we’ve fostered growth and collaboration through 13 locations and inclusive programs. Our vision is a technology-empowered Philippines for all.

What to expect

Volunteering with DEVCON is dynamic: a fun, passionate team, hands-on tasks, problem-solving, and a lot of networking with speakers, sponsors, and attendees.

The attendee experience comes first. Content, seating, audio, and the overall flow all matter.
DEVCON is a safe space for everyone. We have zero tolerance for harassment. Events with children strictly follow the Child Protection Policy.

What to bring

  • A positive attitude and a willingness to learn. This matters most.
  • A notebook and pen for instructions and observations.
  • A charged phone and power bank for team communication.
  • A reusable water bottle. Stay hydrated.
  • Comfortable shoes. You’ll be on your feet.
  • Extra snacks, just in case.

Before the event

  1. Know your role. Your event lead assigns you to Logistics, Meals, Marketing and Creatives, Program, or Documentation. Ask senior volunteers if anything is unclear.
  2. Attend the volunteer briefing. Meet your team, learn the event flow, and clarify tasks.
  3. Study the event plan. Know the program, checklist, and floor plan.
  4. Plan for risks. Projector fails? Long registration line? Always have a contingency.
  5. Align with leaders on sponsor and partner commitments. For sponsored events, follow the BIR invoice guideline for tax compliance.

On the day

Arrive early. Show up at your call time, ideally 2–4 hours before the event for ingress and contingency.

Pre-event setup

  • Eat before heading to the venue
  • Banners and signage correctly set up
  • Projector adapter tested
  • Wi-Fi password tested for speakers and volunteers
  • Volunteer group chat active

Program and content

  • Speaker slides pre-loaded with the right access
  • Digital copies of the registration list and speaker bios
  • Reminders, location, and instructions sent to speakers
  • Speakers on time and coordinated, with tokens and water ready
  • Hosts briefed on the full program flow
  • Looping video or background music playing during registration
  • Content team ready for teasers, “happening now” posts, group photos, and thank-yous

Contingency and raffle

  • Plan B ready for technical glitches
  • Key risks and mitigations understood
  • Raffle system (like Wheel of Names) set up

At the registration desk and on the floor

  • Registration: be welcoming, check names, hand out kits, and stay calm through the first-hour rush.
  • Greeters and ushers: guide attendees to sessions, restrooms, and food.
  • Session facilitators: help speakers, manage mics for Q&A, and assist hands-on activities.
  • Team communication: report issues in the group chat right away.

After the event

  1. Tidy up. Pack materials, remove signage, and leave the venue as you found it.
  2. Debrief. Share what went well and what to improve.
  3. Reflect. Note what you learned and what you’d do differently.
  4. Stay connected. Many lasting friendships and careers started at DEVCON events.

Best practices from our 13 locations

  • Underpromise, overdeliver. Set realistic expectations, then exceed them.
  • Take initiative. See something that needs doing? Ask your lead if you can help.
  • Be a problem-solver. Stay calm and communicate solutions.
  • Be the face of DEVCON. Approachable, helpful, professional.
  • Remember the human connection. Make every attendee feel welcome.
  • Prepare for anything. Extra power bank, pen, and a small bag.
  • Network well: connect on LinkedIn, listen more than you talk, have your elevator pitch ready, and invite more volunteers.

Event rescheduling and weather protocol

Safety comes first, especially during the rainy season. We decide on cancellations at least 1–2 days before the event.

  1. Monitor conditions: leads and logistics track storm signals, rainfall advisories, and flooding on travel routes.
  2. Consult stakeholders: chapter officers, department heads, venue partners, and traveling speakers.
  3. Make the call on safety: a collective decision, then an official announcement on all channels.
  4. Communicate directly: the program team informs speakers and hosts; logistics coordinates with venues and sponsors.

Options, from lightest to heaviest: adjust the program, go hybrid, reschedule, or cancel.

Thank you for your dedication. We hope that in 5 to 10 years, you’ll look back on this volunteer opportunity with pride.

Questions about this policy? Email hello@devcon.ph.

Community Playbook

Code of Conduct for National and Chapter Officers and Volunteers

DevConnect Philippines Inc. (DEVCON Philippines) is committed to a safe, inclusive, and welcoming environment. This code sets the expected behavior of everyone who organizes events and engages the tech community on DEVCON’s behalf.

On this page

  • Core principles
  • Specific expectations
  • Data privacy, photos, and safe space
  • Contact and reporting
  • Anti-bribery and corruption
  • Consequences of violation

Core principles

  • Respect: treat everyone with dignity, regardless of background, experience, gender, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, religion, disability, or any other personal characteristic.
  • Diversity and inclusion: encourage participation from all and actively combat discrimination and harassment.
  • Professionalism: online and offline, avoid profanity, insults, and disruptive behavior.
  • Transparency: in communication and decision-making.
  • Zero tolerance for corruption, bullying, and toxic organizational culture.

Specific expectations

Event organization

  • Keep every event inclusive and welcoming.
  • Promote a safe and respectful environment.
  • Publish a clear Code of Conduct for every event.
  • Have a clear plan for handling misconduct reports.

Community engagement

  • Be respectful and inclusive online and offline.
  • Use your position to promote diversity and inclusion.
  • Avoid posting anything offensive or discriminatory.
  • Uphold DEVCON’s values in every interaction.

Financial integrity

  • Uphold the highest standards of financial responsibility and transparency.
  • Report suspected financial misconduct to the national office and accounting team.

Bullying and harassment

  • Do not tolerate bullying or harassment, in person or online.
  • Make it safe for anyone to report incidents.
  • Act immediately on every report.

Healthy community environment

  • Promote a positive, collaborative culture in leadership and chapters.
  • Avoid gossip and negativity.
  • Foster open communication and respect for diverse viewpoints.

Data privacy, photos, and safe space

  • Your information: unless stated in the event consent form, we will not share personal information like your name and email with partners and sponsors. See the Data Privacy Notice (opens in a new tab).
  • Photography and video: documentation teams capture photos and videos for promotion. Attending means you consent to your likeness being used.
  • Safe and respectful environment: harassment, discrimination, and threats are not tolerated.
  • Safety and responsibility: we do our best to keep events safe; attending means accepting the inherent risks of any event.

Contact and reporting

  • Local events are organized by individual chapters. Contact the organizing chapter’s Facebook page.
  • National events and summits: email hello@devcon.ph.
Reporting misconduct: if you experience or witness a violation, report it immediately to a member of the DEVCON leadership team. Every report is taken seriously and investigated confidentially. Anonymous reporting is available.

Anti-bribery and corruption

Uphold the highest ethical standards with national, local, and global development agencies, government bodies, LGUs, and other organizations. We have zero tolerance for bribery and corruption.

  • Gifts and hospitality: never offer, give, solicit, or accept bribes, kickbacks, or improper payments. Gifts must be reasonable and never meant to influence decisions.
  • Conflicts of interest: disclose any potential conflict to the national office immediately.
  • Record-keeping: keep accurate records; external financial dealings must be documented and approved.
  • Reporting: report suspected bribery confidentially. Retaliation against good-faith reporters is not tolerated.

Consequences of violation

Violations may lead to disciplinary action, including:

  • A warning
  • Preventive suspension during investigation
  • Removal from the leadership position
  • A ban from future DEVCON events and roles

By following this code, officers and volunteers help build a Philippine tech community that is welcoming, inclusive, free from corruption and bullying, and respectful of privacy.

Questions about this policy? Email hello@devcon.ph.

What you agree to when you register for or attend a DEVCON event, in plain language.

On this page

Data privacy and consent

  • Marketing and announcements: attending or completing our form means you agree to receive DEVCON news and event announcements. To be removed, email hello@devcon.ph with the event details.
  • Full policy: read the DEVCON Data Privacy Notice (opens in a new tab).
  • Documentation on site: photos and videos may be taken for promotional purposes. Your attendance indicates consent.

Safe space and event risk

  • Safe and respectful environment: by attending, you help us keep DEVCON welcoming and respectful. Harassment, discrimination, and threats are not tolerated.
  • Safety and responsibility: we do our best to keep events safe; by attending, you accept the inherent risks of any event.

Contact

  • Local events: organized by individual chapters. Contact the organizing chapter’s Facebook page, or find it on our Chapters page.
  • National events: for summits and national-office events, email hello@devcon.ph.

Home/Community Playbook/Campus DEVCON Events Guidelines
Community Playbook

Best Practices for Campus DEVCON Events

Dear chapter leaders: the community sees DEVCON events as the gold standard. These HQ guidelines turn nationwide retrospectives into operational excellence, so every campus event stays world-class.

On this page

  • I. Underpromise and overdeliver
  • II. Creative fundraising and partnerships
  • III. Content strategy and slides
  • IV. Program management
  • V. Speaker and sponsor relations
  • VI. Safety and emergencies
  • VII. Final readiness checklist

I. Underpromise and overdeliver

  • Assume risks by default. Plan as if the internet will fail, a speaker will be late, and power will fluctuate.
  • Build strategic buffers of 10–15 minutes so you never cut a speaker’s slot.
  • Commit conservatively. Never promise a partner an attendance number unless you’re sure you can hit 120% of it.
  • Keep a safe space. Follow the HQ Safe Space Guidelines and the Code of Conduct.

II. Creative fundraising and partnerships

DEVCON is a 17-year-old brand. Use that credibility.

  • Plan 3–6 months ahead. The biggest costs are raffle items, speaker tokens, and organizer meals.
  • Target budget cycles: partner with local DOST, DICT, or school IT organizations during peak cycles like IT Week.
  • Start with a proposal: find official emails of local representatives and send a professional collaboration proposal.
  • Prioritize in-kind sponsorships over cash, due to tax and legal risk. Look for win-win “X-deals”.

III. Content strategy and slides

  • Diverse topics: quantum computing, generative AI, web3 and blockchain, robotics, cybersecurity, DevOps, and tech leadership.
  • One master slide file to avoid flash-drive and permission issues.
  • Decks due 3–4 days before, with a calendar reminder to speakers.
  • Collaborate in Canva or Google Slides so the tech team can check content and aspect ratios early.

IV. Program management

  • Play the DEVCON loop during registration and breaks (see the Community Playbook).
  • Arrive 3–4 hours early (4–6 for large summits) for rehearsals and safety checks.
  • Tech-check every speaker: audio, clicker, transitions.
  • Energetic, rehearsed hosts who manage transitions smoothly.

V. Speaker and sponsor relations

  • Professional impression: your speaker might be your future employer.
  • Speaker integrity is non-negotiable: never drop a speaker on the day. Shorten breaks or Q&A instead.
  • Logistics 14 days prior: a calendar invite with a map pin, gate number, building, and parking.
  • A dedicated liaison for every guest, from entrance to holding area.
  • Quality appreciation: professionally printed certificates and quality tokens, never flimsy bond paper.

VI. Safety and emergencies

  • Open with a 60-second safety brief: nearest exits and medical station.
  • Technical redundancy: backup laptop, spare clicker, and a secondary internet source.
  • Contingency protocols for speaker no-shows, power outages, and medical emergencies.

VII. Final readiness checklist

2–6 months before

  • Local DOST, DICT, and school reps contacted
  • Venue confirmed, electrical and A/V capacity verified
  • Promotions live for at least 3 weeks
  • Partner and co-presenter roles defined
  • In-kind deals for meals, raffle, and tokens secured
  • Volunteer briefing 2–4 days before
  • E-certificates designed and delivery tested

Speakers and content

  • All decks submitted 3–4 days before
  • Final logistics invite sent (map, call time, parking)
  • Liaisons briefed on all VIPs
  • Looping videos downloaded

Technical and risk

  • All presentations in one master file
  • Projector and sound tested (16:9 / 4:3, mic batteries)
  • Mobile hotspot ready as Plan B
  • Fire exits clear, safety officer assigned
  • All volunteers briefed on Safe Space policies
Most importantly: have fun! Energy is contagious. After the event, share your learnings so every chapter grows together.

Questions about this policy? Email hello@devcon.ph.

DEVCON Philippines Child Protection Policy

Our commitment to keeping every child safe in DEVCON Kids programs, activities, and events, online and offline.

On this page

  • 1. Introduction
  • 2. Scope
  • 3. Guiding principles
  • 4. Child protection procedures
  • 5. Reporting concerns
  • 6. Contact
  • 7. Disciplinary action
  • 8. Accessibility

1. Introduction

DEVCON Philippines, the country’s largest community of IT students, developers, and tech enthusiasts across 13 locations, is committed to a safe, inclusive environment for every child in our programs. As a non-profit empowering the next generation of Filipino tech talent, we recognize our responsibility to protect children from harm, abuse, and exploitation, especially in DEVCON Kids, which makes computer science accessible and fun. This policy is the framework for everyone working with children in the program.

2. Scope

This policy applies to everyone involved with DEVCON Kids:

  • Staff (paid and unpaid) working directly with DEVCON Kids
  • Volunteers
  • Board members overseeing DEVCON Kids
  • Contractors
  • Partners
  • Interns
  • Anyone else working with children in the program

It covers all DEVCON Kids activities: coding classes and workshops, competitions, expos, events, online interactions, and communications with children.

3. Guiding principles

  • Paramountcy of the child: the child’s best interests come first in every decision.
  • Prevention: a culture of safeguarding, with awareness of online and technology risks.
  • Protection from physical, emotional, and sexual abuse, neglect, and exploitation, with attention to online safety.
  • Participation: children may express their views in decisions that affect them.
  • Equality and inclusion for every child, regardless of background, ethnicity, gender, or ability.
  • Accountability and transparency in our safeguarding practices.

4. Child protection procedures

  • Recruitment and screening: safe recruitment, including background checks where permissible, references, and interviews.
  • Training: mandatory training on this policy, online safety, digital citizenship, and appropriate virtual interactions, with regular refreshers.
  • Code of Conduct: clear guidelines on physical contact, online and offline communication, confidentiality, and boundaries.
  • Supervision appropriate to each child’s age and the activity, with heightened attention online.
  • Online safety: age-appropriate platforms, protection from cyberbullying and inappropriate content, and data privacy.
  • Reporting: clear, accessible procedures; every report is investigated promptly.
  • Confidentiality for children and families, within our legal obligations to report.
  • Record keeping: accurate, confidential records of concerns.
  • Partnerships only with organizations that share our commitment.
  • Policy review in line with Philippine law and best practice.

5. Reporting concerns

Any concern or suspicion of abuse or neglect, including online safety violations, must be reported immediately to DEVCON Philippines’ designated Child Protection Officer(s). Reports may also be made to the appropriate authorities as required by law.

6. Contact

For any child protection concern related to DEVCON Kids, email hello@devcon.ph.

7. Disciplinary action

Failure to comply with this policy may result in disciplinary action, including termination of employment or volunteer status.

8. Accessibility

This policy is available to all staff, volunteers, partners, children, and families in appropriate formats and languages. It is a living document, reviewed and updated regularly.

Questions about this policy? Email hello@devcon.ph.

Why representation matters

Close the widest STEM gender gap in Asia-Pacific

Women make up only 28% of the global tech workforce. In the Philippines, women are 36.3% of the STEM workforce, the widest STEM gender gap in the Asia-Pacific region. We’re here to change that.

  • 28%women in the global tech workforce
  • 36.3%women in the Philippine STEM workforce
  • 50%our vision for women in STEM leadership

Our mission

Empower Filipino women and girls to pursue and succeed in technology through accessible education, mentorship, and a supportive community that breaks down systemic barriers.

Our vision

A diverse, inclusive, and equitable Philippine tech industry, with women making up at least 50% of STEM leadership and workforce nationwide.

DEVCON CREST · Climate Resilience Technology

Climate Bayanihan: tech for a climate-resilient Philippines

CREST brings government, business, academe, startups, accelerators, donors, and volunteers together on climate challenges, through a tripartite agreement between DOST, DEVCON, and DLSU.

Join the climate agendaPartner with us
  • 3Tripartite partners: DOST, DEVCON, DLSU
  • Feb 272025 Climate Innovation Leaders Workshop
From San Francisco to Manila

The Climate Innovation Leaders Workshop

After a pilot at San Francisco Tech Week, DEVCON, DLSU, and DOST convened leaders from Metro Manila to Iloilo and Bukidnon at DLSU’s Henry Sy Hall, inspired by DEVCON founder Winston Damarillo’s work with the World Economic Forum.

  • The RISE framework: Research, Incubation, Scale, and Expansion, applied to education, entrepreneurship, and sustainable growth.
  • A “reverse pitch”: DENR presented real-world climate challenges for participants to solve.
  • Speakers from DOST, DENR’s Climate Change Service, and the Board of Investments.
  • Community leaders from New Energy Nexus, Villgro Philippines, Plastic Bank, and UNDP Accelerator Lab.

FAQ

Before you apply

Who can apply?

Filipino developers and builders of any background, language, framework, or stack, anywhere in the Philippines. It isn’t limited to Manila or any single chapter.

Is the review track free?

Yes. The Claude certification review track is self-paced, free, and open to all skill levels.

What does the scholarship cover?

One fully paid attempt at the Claude Certification Exam for applicants who complete the program requirements and pass the mock exams.

How many exam attempts are covered?

One. Take your time to study and review the exam guidelines closely before your official attempt.

How do I secure a slot?

Pass the mock exam three times to show you’re ready, then submit your progress. Selected applicants receive a separate email with access to the official exam.

What happens after I’m certified?

DEVCON connects certified builders to AI Engineering work through our nationwide network.
